gallery.title: Built with SuperDocs
gallery.standfirst: Projects that used SuperDocs to do real work on a real document. Every entry is submitted by the person who built it, and every entry links to something you can open and check.

_note_on_size: This gallery opens with one entry. That is the honest state of it: entries are submitted by their owners and verified against a written bar, and exactly one project has met it so far. Padding the list with builds whose owners never asked to be listed would make the badge mean less, which is the only thing the gallery has to protect.

entries.name: Tracked changes disappear when a document round-trips through markdown
entries.summary: A note on why w:ins, w:del and comment anchors don't survive a conversion through markdown, and a two-line check for whether your own pipeline drops them.
superdocs_surfaces: Editing inside the document (POST /v1/chat) — drafted the caveat in the testing section
HTML export of the finished document

evidence.what: The study the page was built from, with all fifteen source pages linked and their engagement numbers.

entries.reviewer_note: Meets the bar: the page is public, SuperDocs drafted content into a named section while the rest stayed put, and the study behind it is published with its sources linked. The sentence SuperDocs wrote was kept; I moved it to the position I had asked for, which it ignored.
entries.conflict: Submitted and reviewed by the same person — this is the curator's own project. Held to the same three tests as anything else, and disclosed here because the disclosure is the only thing that keeps a one-entry gallery honest.

not_listed.name: This gallery, and the badge it hands out
not_listed.why: It is the gallery, so R5 applies whatever else is true of it. Stated precisely rather than flatteringly: SuperDocs was used on this project — the curation rule was revised through the API and exported — but both sentences it drafted were rejected on review and the one that shipped was written by hand. A gallery that lists itself to look busier is the exact failure the bar exists to prevent.
